messages:
tom: hey team, running into a really odd Safari-only issue with our streaming SSE endpoint. Chrome/Firefox are fine, but on iOS Safari the EventSource connection opens and then after ~15-30s it just… stops sending more events even though server keeps streaming. client sees partial response. :confused:

lucy: hey @tom, thanks for the report — can you paste minimal repro steps and any headers you see? is this behind a CDN/edge?

tom: yep behind Cloudfront + a lightweight CDN layer. repro steps:
1) open the page in Safari on iPhone
2) connect to /v1/stream?session=abc with token in Authorization header (we use a preflight OPTIONS that includes Authorization)
3) server streams SSE events continuously (one event every second)

curl I used to emulate:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.example.com/v1/stream?session=abc'
```

server logs show continuous writes, but client stops after partial chunk. Network tab shows last response as 304 at some point for the endpoint (??).

lucy: 304 on an SSE endpoint is suspicious. SSE should never be cached as a 304. Are you seeing any conditional requests (If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since) from the edge?

tom: yes sometimes the edge issues an If-None-Match upstream and Cloudfront returns 304 from cache. We tried adding Cache-Control: no-cache on origin but CDN seemed to ignore for some paths.

mike: tagging in @ana — this looks like two interacting problems: 1) CDN/edge returning a 304 for a stream, which will abruptly terminate the chunked transfer semantics clients expect, and 2) Safari's EventSource has historically been brittle with streams that get transformed (gzip/content-length changed) or where the connection is torn and reissued as a conditional request by the CDN. Safari often doesn't re-open or handles partial buffered chunks differently.

ana: (sorry typo) ana: echoing that. Quick checklist:
- origin must serve SSE with 200 and Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Content-Type: text/event-stream, no Content-Length, and no intermediate 304 responses.
- CDN must be configured to bypass caching for SSE endpoints or set Cache-Control: private, no-transform, max-age=0.
- preflight should allow Authorization and not be cached.

lucy: @tom can you confirm your origin headers currently? Also do you put Vary headers on for Authorization or cookies?

tom: origin headers currently:
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Connection: keep-alive
```
Vary: Accept-Encoding, Origin
Preflight OPTIONS returns: Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type

lucy: ok Vary does not include Authorization. That might cause edge to incorrectly serve cached 304s for different tokens.

mike: exactly. If the edge is caching an OPTIONS/GET combo and then responding with a 304 for a GET with a different token, the client will get incomplete stream frames. Safari's EventSource will sometimes treat the mid-stream 304 as EOF and not reconnect, leaving you with a partial event buffer.

eve: another subtlety — some CDNs apply gzip/brotli (Content-Encoding) or 'response body reserialization' (no-transform) which can change chunk boundaries. Safari's parser expects event lines separated by \n and can drop partial fragments if chunking changes mid-stream. Use no-transform to avoid encoding changes.

ana: recommended changes we usually push for streaming endpoints:
- Ensure origin sets Cache-Control: private, no-transform, no-cache
- Add Vary: Authorization (so edge keys cache by auth) OR configure CDN rule to bypass cache for /v1/stream*
- Ensure CDN honors origin's no-cache/no-store for that path (bypass edge cache).
- For CORS: ensure OPTIONS and GET responses include Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: the requesting origin (not '*') and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials if you rely on cookies. Note EventSource doesn't support credentials: true, so prefer token-in-query if you need credential-like behavior or put token in header and ensure CDN doesn't cache across tokens.

lucy: thanks @ana & @mike. @tom, possible quick workaround: try hitting the stream with token in query param (temporary) so CDN sees the URL difference, or temporarily disable edge caching for that path and confirm Safari behavior. Also try adding "Cache-Control: no-transform".

tom: ok I'll try disabling edge cache for that path and add Vary: Authorization and no-transform. Any logs I should capture from Safari?

mike: capture the HAR/network export from Safari (Desktop Safari devtools or iOS via macos proxy), but also check edge logs for conditional requests. We want to see if the edge issued an If-None-Match to origin and then returned 304 to client. If true, that's the culprit.

tom: did the change — set CDN rule to bypass cache for /v1/stream*, added Vary: Authorization on origin and Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform. Retested on iPhone Safari. Looks stable now, no mid-stream stop for ~5 mins so far. :tada:

lucy: awesome! marking as likely CDN cache/304-induced. We'll keep thread open for 24h to confirm. Any followups on server side we should implement permanently?

mike: long-term we recommend:
- explicit CDN bypass for SSE endpoints (no caching)
- origin enforce Vary: Authorization if you can't bypass CDN rules
- make SSE endpoints idempotent and use 200 chunked responses (no conditional 304)
- avoid relying on Accept-Encoding transforms, set no-transform

eve: adding a short note to devex docs about Safari and CDN interplay for streaming endpoints — I'll include a small troubleshooting snippet.

deploy-bot: applied temporary CDN rule to bypass cache for /v1/stream on staging at 2026-03-15T14:23Z

lucy: thanks everyone. @tom if you see any regression ping us here and include a network HAR or edge request ids. closing after 24h if stable. :thumbsup:
